//: A composite index does not exist until somebody creates it, and until it
exists the query that needs it fails outright — which made a fresh project
unusable for anyone who could not run the Firebase CLI. Every query in the
app was therefore reduced to a shape Firestore indexes automatically: a
single equality, a single range, or a single orderBy. Where a second key
was wanted (chats by recency, a resident's own reports by date, similar
reports by category) the query fetches a capped page and the app sorts or
filters it locally. The sets involved are a village's worth of data, so the
cost is nothing and the setup step disappears.
Add an entry here only alongside a query that genuinely cannot be shaped
this way, and expect it to need `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes`

fieldOverrides.//: Nothing queries these large arrays; skipping the index saves write cost.
